figureObjective: Show how a uniformly rotating N-turn coil in a magnetic field converts mechanical input into sinusoidal electrical output through changing flux and induced emf.

claims.text: Charges in the two vertical wire segments experience forces parallel to the wire and drive current through a connected external circuit; top and bottom segment forces do not drive current.
The generator converts mechanical energy supplied at the shaft into electrical energy.
Rotating the coil changes magnetic flux and induces an emf that drives current through the external circuit.
For N turns of area A rotating at constant angular velocity omega in uniform field B, epsilon = N A B omega sin(omega t), with peak epsilon0 = N A B omega.
The output alternates with period T = 2 pi / omega; B uses tesla, A square metres, omega radians per second, emf volts, and T seconds if numeric values are introduced.

elements.meaning: Uniform magnetic field B across the rotating coil.
N-turn coil of area A rotating at constant angular velocity omega.
Two coil sides where magnetic force is parallel to the wire and drives current.
Mechanical rotation supplied to the generator shaft.
Connected external circuit receiving the induced alternating current.
Sinusoidal induced emf with peak epsilon0 and period T.

allowedVariation.rule: The coil mechanism and waveform may be arranged side-by-side or sequentially if mechanical input, field, current path, and time relation stay explicit.
Field, force, current, and rotation arrows may use different colors if every vector type has an unambiguous legend.

mutations.description: Show constant nonzero emf for constant-speed rotation or place a peak where the sine relation requires a zero crossing.
Make forces in the top and bottom wire segments the source of loop current while omitting the vertical-side contribution.
Reverse the magnetic-field direction without updating force/current arrows, or disconnect the coil from the depicted load while claiming current through it.
